content.summary_tldr: Find Bluetooth Device is a free iOS app (24.2 MB, iOS 17.1+) that locates lost Bluetooth devices — AirPods, earbuds, headphones, smartwatches and speakers — using signal strength. Unlike Apple Find My, it needs no prior setup and works with any powered-on Bluetooth device, including non-Apple gear. Pick a device from the scan list and follow hot–cold guidance plus a proximity percentage until you find it.
content.intro1: Lost your AirPods somewhere in the house? Earbuds swallowed by the sofa? Find Bluetooth Device is a Bluetooth finder app that scans nearby Bluetooth signals and walks you straight to any powered-on device in range — no Find My network, no iCloud account, and no prior pairing required.
content.intro2: It works like a metal detector for your gadgets: choose the device from the scan list, then move around while the app tells you if you are getting hotter or colder. A live proximity percentage confirms you are closing in, and device details (name, manufacturer, model) make sure you are chasing the right gadget in a room full of Bluetooth signals.

features.title: The Bluetooth Finder for Earbuds, Headphones & AirPods
features.subtitle: Built for one job: getting a lost Bluetooth device back in your hands, fast.

items.title: Instant Bluetooth Scanner
items.description: One tap scans every powered-on Bluetooth device in range and lists it with live signal strength. AirPods, earbuds, headphones, smartwatches, fitness trackers, speakers — if it broadcasts Bluetooth, it shows up.

items.title: Hot & Cold Guidance
items.description: Move around and the app tells you Cold, Warm, Hot or Very Hot based on the live signal. It turns a frustrating search into a two-minute game you always win.

items.title: Proximity Percentage
items.description: A precise percentage indicator shows exactly how close you are. Watch it climb from 40% to 95% as you approach the couch cushion your earbud fell into.

items.title: Device Details That Prevent Wild Chases
items.description: See name, manufacturer and model for every detected device, so you track your AirPods Pro — not your neighbor's TV — even in crowded places with dozens of signals.

items.title: No Setup, No Network, No Account
items.description: Nothing to configure before you lose something. The app finds devices by their live Bluetooth signal, so it works with secondhand AirPods, non-Apple earbuds and gadgets that were never in Find My.

items.title: Works Where You Actually Lose Things
items.description: Homes, offices, gyms, cars, trains and cafés. Bluetooth range is roughly 10–30 meters indoors — exactly the radius where most devices go missing.

how_it_works.title: How It Works
how_it_works.subtitle: From download to found device in about two minutes.

steps.title: Download the app
steps.description: Get Find Bluetooth Device free from the App Store. It needs iOS 17.1 or later and takes 24.2 MB — a few seconds on Wi-Fi.

steps.title: Scan for nearby devices
steps.description: Open the app and start a scan. Every powered-on Bluetooth device in range appears in a list with its signal strength.

steps.title: Pick the device you lost
steps.description: Identify your device by its name, manufacturer or model. Not sure which one it is? The strongest unnamed signal that follows you between rooms is usually it.

steps.title: Follow hot–cold guidance
steps.description: Walk slowly around the area. The app shifts from Cold to Warm to Hot as the signal strengthens, and the proximity percentage climbs as you close in.

steps.title: Pinpoint and grab it
steps.description: At Very Hot and 90%+, your device is within arm's reach. Check cushions, pockets, bags and drawers right around you.

faq.question: What is Find Bluetooth Device?
faq.answer: Find Bluetooth Device is a free iOS app that locates lost Bluetooth devices using their live signal. It scans for nearby AirPods, earbuds, headphones, smartwatches, fitness trackers and speakers, then guides you to the one you pick with a hot–cold indicator and a proximity percentage. It requires iOS 17.1 or later and is 24.2 MB.
faq.learn_more_text: Learn more: All Bluetooth Finder Guides →

faq.question: How do I find lost AirPods with my iPhone?
faq.answer: If Find My was set up, start there — it shows a map location and can play a sound. If your AirPods aren't in Find My, or Find My only shows a vague location, scan for them with Find Bluetooth Device: while AirPods are outside the case and powered on, they broadcast a Bluetooth signal you can follow room by room until you're within arm's reach.
faq.learn_more_text: Learn more: How to Find Lost AirPods →

faq.question: Can I find AirPods without Find My or iCloud?
faq.answer: Yes. AirPods broadcast Bluetooth whenever they're out of the case and powered on, and Find Bluetooth Device tracks that signal directly — no Find My network, iCloud account or prior pairing needed. This also works for secondhand AirPods still linked to the previous owner's Apple Account.
faq.learn_more_text: Learn more: Find AirPods Without Find My →

faq.question: Can I find just one lost AirPod?
faq.answer: Yes. Each AirPod broadcasts its own Bluetooth signal while it's out of the case and charged. Scan with the app, select your AirPods from the list, and follow the hot–cold guidance — the proximity percentage will spike when you're right on top of the missing earbud.
faq.learn_more_text: Learn more: Find One Lost AirPod →

faq.question: Can I find AirPods or earbuds with a dead battery?
faq.answer: No Bluetooth finder can detect a device whose battery is fully dead, because it no longer broadcasts a signal. Check Find My for the last known location, search there, and re-scan periodically — earbuds sometimes wake briefly with residual charge. Installing a Bluetooth finder before your next loss means you can catch devices while they still have battery.
faq.learn_more_text: Learn more: How to Find Dead AirPods →

faq.question: Does it work with non-Apple headphones like Sony, Bose or Beats?
faq.answer: Yes. Find Bluetooth Device works with any brand — Sony, Bose, Beats, JBL, Sennheiser and more — because it reads the standard Bluetooth signal every wireless headphone broadcasts while powered on. Most non-Apple headphones can't be tracked with Find My at all, which makes signal tracking the main way to find them.
faq.learn_more_text: Learn more: Find Lost Bluetooth Headphones →

faq.question: Can it find Galaxy Buds, Jabra and other earbuds?
faq.answer: Yes. Any earbuds that are powered on and in Bluetooth range appear in the scan list with their signal strength, regardless of brand. Select them and follow the hot–cold guidance to their hiding spot.

faq.question: Can I find a lost smartwatch or fitness tracker?
faq.answer: Yes. Smartwatches and fitness bands like Fitbit, Garmin and Amazfit broadcast Bluetooth almost constantly, which makes them reliable targets. Scan, select your watch by name or manufacturer, and walk toward the strongest signal.
faq.learn_more_text: Learn more: Find a Lost Smartwatch →

faq.question: Can I find a lost Bluetooth speaker like JBL, Bose or Anker?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as it's powered on. Speakers have stronger Bluetooth transmitters than earbuds, so they often show up from across the whole house. Scan, pick your speaker from the list and follow the hot–cold guidance room by room until the proximity percentage peaks.
faq.learn_more_text: Learn more: Find a Lost Bluetooth Speaker →

faq.question: Can I find a lost AirPods case?
faq.answer: Sometimes. A closed case with the earbuds inside is asleep and doesn't broadcast, and an empty standard case has no active transmitter. But if the lid is open, the earbuds inside wake and advertise, and a scan can pick them up. AirPods Pro 2 and later cases also support Find My.
faq.learn_more_text: Learn more: Find a Lost AirPods Case →

faq.question: How accurate is the proximity tracking?
faq.answer: The app converts live signal strength into a percentage and a hot–cold level. Bluetooth signal isn't GPS — it can't give an exact map pin — but within its 10–30 meter indoor range it reliably narrows the search to arm's reach: Very Hot with 90%+ means the device is right around you.
faq.learn_more_text: Learn more: How Bluetooth Signal Strength Works →

faq.question: Is Find Bluetooth Device free?
faq.answer: Yes, the app is free to download from the App Store and includes an optional premium subscription with a free trial. It requires iOS 17.1 or later on iPhone and takes 24.2 MB of storage.
faq.learn_more_text: Learn more: Start Finding Your Device →

faq.question: How is this different from Apple Find My?
faq.answer: Find My tracks Apple devices that were registered to your Apple Account before they were lost, and can locate them far away via its network. Find Bluetooth Device needs no registration and works with any brand, but only while the device is powered on and within Bluetooth range. In practice: use Find My to get to the right building, and a Bluetooth finder to get to the right couch cushion.
faq.learn_more_text: Learn more: Finding Devices Without Find My →

faq.question: Can I see all Bluetooth devices near me?
faq.answer: Yes. The scan list shows every powered-on Bluetooth device in range with its signal strength, and device details show the name, manufacturer and model when available — useful for identifying unknown devices around you as well as finding your own.
faq.learn_more_text: Learn more: Bluetooth Scanner for iPhone →
